case_name: Mehta Ravindrarai Ajitrai (Deceased) Through His Heirs and Lrs and Others v State Of Gujarat
petitioner: Mehta Ravindrarai Ajitrai (Deceased) Through His Heirs and Lrs and Others
respondent:
State Of Gujarat
Supreme Court of India

8 August 1989
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION: Civil Appeal No. 2169 of 1970. From the Judgment and Order dated 12.8.68 of the Gujarat High Court in F.A. No. 233 of 1963
The Judgment was delivered by : M. H. Kania, J.

facts: This is an appeal by special leave granted by this Court under Article 136 of the Constitution.

The acquisition was in respect of an area admeasuring 15 acres and 1 guntha belonging to claimant No. 1 (Original) and area admeasuring 6 acres and 25 gunthas belonging to claimant Nos. 1 and 2 (Original).
The lands are situated in the Bhavnagar District and are on the outskirts of the Bhavnagar City and adjoining the Bhavnagar Rajkot Road.
The preliminary notification under section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was published on August 6, 1956.
issues: Whether the High Court was justified in not taking into account the instance reflected in the sale deed (Exhibit 152) and the agreement for sale in connection with that land.
What is the market value of a piece of property for purposes of section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act?
petitioner_arguments: The claimants had made their claim at Rs.3 per sq. yard before the Land Acquisition Officer.
The agreement to sell dated January 21, 1957 must be regarded as furnishing some light on the market value of the land on the date of publication of section 4 notification.
respondent_arguments: The High Court inter alia rejected this instance on the basis that the contents of the sale deed were not properly proved.
The State examined one Virbhadrasingh on whose behalf the land was purchased under the said sale deed (Exhibit 118).
court_reasoning: Keeping these factors in mind, we feel that although the instance reflected in the sale deed (Exhibit 152) and the agreement for sale in connection with that land, pertains to a sale after the acquisition, it can be fairly regarded as reasonably proximate to the acquisition.
We find that the High Court placed reliance on the evidence furnished by the instances at Exhibit 112 relied on by the State.
holding: The market value of the acquired land is fixed at Rs.8,800 per acre which comes to about Rs.1.80 per sq. yard.
The decree passed by the Civil Judge, Senior Division, Bhavnagar will be amended accordingly.
